# Ezra Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 468r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EZR_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** In the first year of King Cyrus of Persia — so that the LORD's word spoken through Jeremiah would be fulfilled — the LORD moved the heart of Cyrus to issue a proclamation throughout his entire kingdom. He also put it in writing:

**2** "This is what King Cyrus of Persia declares: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth and has appointed me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, in the land of Judah. **3** Anyone among you who belongs to his people — may God be with you! — go up to Jerusalem in Judah and rebuild the temple of the LORD, the God of Israel, the God who dwells in Jerusalem. **4** And wherever survivors are living, let the people of that place provide them with silver, gold, supplies, and livestock, along with freewill offerings for the temple of God in Jerusalem."

**5** Then the leaders of the families of Judah and Benjamin, together with the priests and Levites — everyone whose heart God had moved — set out to go and rebuild the LORD's temple in Jerusalem. **6** All their neighbors helped them with articles of silver and gold, with supplies, livestock, and valuable gifts, in addition to all the freewill offerings.

**7** King Cyrus himself brought out the articles that had belonged to the LORD's temple, the ones Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and placed in the temple of his own gods. **8** Cyrus entrusted them to Mithredath the royal treasurer, who inventoried them for Sheshbazzar, the leader of Judah. **9** Here is the inventory: thirty gold dishes, one thousand silver dishes, twenty-nine knives, **10** thirty gold bowls, four hundred and ten matching silver bowls, and one thousand other articles. **11** In all, there were five thousand four hundred gold and silver articles. Sheshbazzar brought all of these along when the exiles made their journey from Babylon to Jerusalem.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — "The LORD moved the heart":** The Hebrew says "stirred up the spirit" (*he'ir et-ruach*). This is one of the Bible's most remarkable theological claims — that the God of Israel directed the decisions of a pagan emperor. The same God who sent Judah into exile now ends it through a foreign king.

**Verse 2 — Cyrus's theology:** Cyrus speaks of "the LORD, the God of heaven" — language that a Persian king might well have used as a diplomatic courtesy. The Cyrus Cylinder shows he similarly credited Marduk when addressing Babylonians. The biblical author sees genuine divine action behind diplomatic rhetoric.

**Verse 5 — "Everyone whose heart God had moved":** Not all Jews returned. The text is honest about this — only those whom God specifically stirred chose to make the difficult journey. The return was voluntary and partial.

*— PNEUMA*
